title: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
summary: One-arm dumbbell row with a hand on a bench: lats 1, upper back 0.8. Long range per side, little lower-back load.

muscles.why: The lats pull the upper arm back toward the hip; one arm at a time gives a long reach.
Rhomboids and mid traps pull the shoulder blade back.
Rear delts help pull the arm back.

setup.text: Hand and knee on a bench, other foot on the floor.
Back flat, about parallel to the floor.

form_cues.cue: Pull the dumbbell toward your hip
Keep your torso square to the floor
form_cues.why: Letting the shoulder reach down at the bottom.

form_cues.cue: Elbow close to the body for lats
form_cues.why: Flaring shifts it to the upper back.

bias_tweaks.change: Elbow flared, pull to the chest
bias_tweaks.effect: More upper back and rear delts.

bias_tweaks.change: Lower in 2-3 seconds and pause briefly in the stretch
bias_tweaks.effect: Keeps tension on in the lengthened position and removes bounce, so each rep starts honestly.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Rep speeds from 0.5 to 8 s gave similar growth; this is a control tool, not a growth trick.

mistakes.text: Twisting the torso open to raise the dumbbell higher.
mistakes.fix: Lighten until the torso stays still.

misconceptions.myth: Every set has to go to failure to grow.
misconceptions.reality: Stopping a few reps short gave similar growth to failure in a meta-analysis; growth tends to rise as sets get closer to failure, but the exact curve is uncertain.

lower_risk.text: The app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the first working load is at least 18 kg (40 lb) per hand and the main muscle is not already warm from an earlier lift. Otherwise start with a slightly lighter first set.

Add load in small steps. The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first, up to 2 past the top of the range. Default steps for this equipment are 2 kg or 5 lb; your gym profile can replace them.
Aim for about 3 reps in reserve in the 8-12 rep range. Easy to push close to failure; stop when you start twisting.
Pick a variation, range and setup you can train comfortably.

alternatives.why: Machine row with the chest supported.
Barbell row: heavier, more upper back.

alternatives.goal_label: Home gym: no equipment / bar only

notes: Row variations have not been compared for growth in a study the app cites.
Ratings and display bands are the library model (main >= 0.75, helper 0.4 to < 0.75, minor 0.25 to < 0.4, not counted < 0.25).
Technique and load management only. This page makes no medical or injury claims.
